name: Mike Collins
profileSummary: Two-term hard-right congressman and trucking company owner running on a MAGA/America First platform; Heritage Action 98%, LCV 1%, sponsor of the Laken Riley Act, and one of the most conservative members of the House delegation.
keyPositions: Sponsored the Laken Riley Act (signed into law Jan 2025) and supports immigration moratorium including reduced legal immigration
Advocates abolishing the ATF, repealing the NFA, and national constitutional carry (GGO 100%, NRA ~92%)
LCV 1% lifetime; calls green energy policies 'ridiculous' and champions 'drill here, drill now'
Voted for One Big Beautiful Bill ($800B Medicaid cuts); told retirees to 'get off Social Security, get back in the workforce'
Cosponsored personhood bill recognizing life at conception; opposes all Planned Parenthood funding

sources: XTRA 106.3 radio interview June 2025 ('get off Social Security')
One Big Beautiful Bill vote (Tier 1) -- $800B Medicaid cuts
iVoterGuide 2022 ('between C and D' on taxpayer-funded healthcare)
econ_safetynet.notes: Explicitly told retirees to 'get off of Social Security, get off of Medicaid, get back in the workforce' on radio in June 2025. Goes beyond standard Republican rhetoric into active advocacy for reducing core safety net programs. iVoterGuide response suggests keeping Medicare/Medicaid in some minimal form (not a full 10), but OBBBA vote and rhetoric point to dramatic reductions.

econ_investment.notes: Consistently opposes public investment and government spending. Voted against the bipartisan debt ceiling deal because it did not cut enough. Business background and anti-government framing are central to identity.

econ_tax_structure.notes: Tax cuts are central to economic worldview. Framed in radio interview as the solution to both economic growth and reducing safety net dependency.

justice_firearms.notes: Maximum pro-gun positioning. Not merely opposing new regulations but actively seeking to abolish the primary federal firearms regulatory agency (ATF) and repeal the foundational firearms law (NFA, 1934). After a mass shooting in his own district that killed 4 people (Apalachee High School, Sept 2024), he maintained 'the problem is not the gun.' This is the most extreme documented firearms position on the scale.

universalism.reasoning: LCV 1% lifetime -- near-total opposition to environmental protection for nature and future generations. Opposed Ukraine military aid (isolationist, not extending concern to global victims). Advocates immigration moratorium including reducing legal immigration -- narrowing the circle of who deserves inclusion. Antisemitism-adjacent social media incident and refusal to delete post suggests indifference to out-group harm. AI deepfake campaign video demonstrates willingness to deceive. Across environmental, international, and immigration domains, consistently acts against universalist values.

benevolence.reasoning: Mixed signals. TRANQ Act (bipartisan fentanyl law) shows genuine concern for communities affected by drug crisis. Laken Riley Act framed as protecting community from violence. Campaign rhetoric emphasizes 'hardworking men and women.' However, voted for OBBBA projected to strip coverage from up to 750K Georgians in his own district. Radio statement telling retirees to 'get off Social Security' directly undermines senior welfare. The rhetoric of care is contradicted by policy actions that harm constituents. Net neutral.

tradition.reasoning: 'Unapologetically pro God' -- explicit religious values framing. Cosponsored personhood bill (life at conception) -- traditional moral values on abortion. Son of former congressman Mac Collins -- political dynasty. Opposes Planned Parenthood funding on moral grounds. Conservative cultural orientation is central to identity. Does not reach 0.8+ because the MAGA movement itself is disruptive of some political traditions (e.g., fiscal conservatism, democratic norms).

conformity.reasoning: Pattern of norm-violating behavior despite high procedural attendance (99% vote participation). Released AI deepfake campaign video depicting opponent -- a serious departure from campaign conduct norms. Approvingly engaged with antisemitic social media account and refused to delete post despite bipartisan rebukes. Under House Ethics Committee investigation for misuse of government funds. Voted against bipartisan debt ceiling deal, defying party leadership. The aggressive, confrontational style ('steamroll the radical left') and willingness to use deceptive tactics place him in anti-conformity territory.

security.reasoning: Strong on physical and border security: finish the wall, Remain in Mexico, immigration moratorium, Laken Riley Act, 'strong military peace through strength.' However, actively undermines economic security for vulnerable populations -- 'get off Social Security,' OBBBA Medicaid cuts. The security orientation is selective: strong for national defense and law enforcement, weak for social safety net security. Net positive because physical security emphasis is more prominent in his political identity.

power.reasoning: Aligned with business power structures: Chamber of Commerce praise, Heritage Foundation near-perfect alignment, tax reform leadership favoring corporate interests. Built personal business empire (1 truck to 115). Trump alignment as power strategy. 'I'm That Guy' primary assertion. Accepts traditional donor/PAC support structure. Orientation is toward maintaining and leveraging existing power hierarchies rather than challenging them.

achievement.reasoning: Self-made entrepreneur narrative is central to identity: built trucking company from one semi-truck to 115 trucks and 100+ employees. Led three businesses, chaired chamber of commerce and credit union board. 'Get back in the workforce' framing treats work and self-sufficiency as moral imperatives. Policy positions consistently emphasize individual effort over structural support. Achievement through personal competence is a defining value.

hedonism.reasoning: Social conservatism (pro-life, 'pro God') implicitly restricts personal lifestyle choices. No libertarian personal freedom emphasis. No positions on recreational cannabis or lifestyle liberty issues. Personhood bill and opposition to Planned Parenthood extend government authority into deeply personal domains. Mildly negative because the overall orientation restricts rather than expands personal pleasure and choice.

stimulation.reasoning: Some anti-establishment energy: defied party leadership on Fiscal Responsibility Act, confrontational rhetoric ('steamroll the radical left'), willingness to use novel AI tactics in campaigns. However, the policy vision is fundamentally restorationist -- 'America First' looks backward to a perceived better past, not forward to novel solutions. Not an innovator or structural reformer; a disruptor in style but conservative in substance.

self_direction.reasoning: Strong individual liberty emphasis in gun rights (abolish ATF, repeal NFA, constitutional carry) and economic domains (anti-regulation, anti-government intervention). However, personhood bill restricts reproductive autonomy. Immigration moratorium restricts freedom of movement. 'Pro God' governance frame suggests willingness to impose moral values through law. The liberty orientation is domain-selective: maximalist on guns and business, restrictive on reproductive choice and immigration. Net slightly positive because gun and economic liberty are more prominent in his active advocacy.

conflicts.description: Campaign rhetoric emphasizes fighting for 'hardworking men and women' of Georgia, but June 2025 radio interview explicitly told retirees to 'get off Social Security, get back in the workforce.' RSC budget proposals he supports would cut Social Security benefits.
conflicts.scoringImpact: Score reflects the radio statement and OBBBA vote (actions/Tier 1-2) over campaign rhetoric (Tier 3). Scored econ_safetynet at 9.

conflicts.description: Describes himself as pro-worker and fighting for Georgians, but voted for One Big Beautiful Bill projected to strip coverage from up to 750,000 GA-10 constituents and raise premiums 345%. CBO independently projects 11.8M national coverage losses.
conflicts.scoringImpact: Partisan source for GA-10 projection, but CBO provides independent corroboration at national level. Scored health_coverage_model at 9.

conflicts.description: Voted AGAINST Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 as too moderate on spending, signaling deficit-hawk credentials. Then voted FOR One Big Beautiful Bill, which CRFB projects adds trillions to the deficit. Heritage Action 98% score masks this tension.
conflicts.scoringImpact: Both votes are Tier 1 evidence. The inconsistency suggests MAGA loyalty trumps fiscal discipline when they conflict. Noted but does not change axis scores since both votes point toward reduced government spending/services.

conflicts.description: Under House Ethics Committee investigation (announced Nov 2025) for alleged misuse of government funds to benefit chief of staff Brandon Phillips, who allegedly hired his girlfriend to work in Collins' office. Collins calls it 'baseless.'
conflicts.scoringImpact: Factored into conformity value score (-0.3). Does not affect policy axis scores.
